title: Trombone lessons, school bands, first jobs and post office rally
summary: Lessons from age 11 on valve then slide trombone, school bands and St. Augustine, joining the union at 17, the Toppers, Dejan's band, and the Zip Codes playing political rallies.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Mm-hmm. And so, uh, did you have any lessons when you were young?

Oh, yeah, I started taking music lessons, uh, when I was about 11 years old. Uh, started out on the vowel trombone. I played the vowel trombone for, uh, uh, four years. And, uh, the reason why my daddy put me on the vowel trombone, because he figured my arm wasn't long enough for the slide to go away on it.

So when I got about the age of, uh, 15, 16 years old, uh, I switched over to the slide trombone, and I still was taking music lessons. Every Saturday for now, uh, Crescent City Music Hall, uh, went down and a half a lesson. And, uh, uh, started taking music lessons in school, playing, uh, in a school band. Uh, I remember I played my first solo when I was at, uh, attending McDonald's number 41. Uh, band director, Mr. Dennis, uh, he gave me an acting role I liked to play a solo, and I did that, uh, school exercise. And, well, it turned out pretty good. I thought it was shaking for the first time. Uh, and then it just went on, uh, after I left, uh, McDonald's 41, uh, went to St. Augustine High School. And, uh, had to go through some red tape to get for an audition to get into that band, because it's really not easy. It's a lot of work. And, uh, a lot of margin, too. Uh, it's, a lot of work. Uh, it's, uh, this, this is where I, I really got a hold of, uh, more ideas for his horn, for his concern, because you never could like, you always had to keep up with your horn, because, uh, the guy right next to you, he's always trying to get you a seat, you know. Mm-hmm. And it was sort of like a challenge. And, uh, so in order to perform, you have to, you have to do your best. And the whole while I was there, I was, I was sitting in the number two seat for four years. Number two seat. There's me and this other guy, a friend of mine, he was playing drum. He was, uh, he was pretty good. He was pretty good, but, uh, there's just some little things, uh, he got me on, but, and some little things I got him on. But, you know, as it went by when I got to the age of seventeen, I joined the musician union. And, uh, played my first, uh, professional job with, with the Toppers Orchestra. Uh, Milton Baptiste, you know. Uh, and, uh, a few months later, I joined Harold DeJong's band. And, uh, I've been, uh, been playing with Harold ever since. We travel around a few places in the country. Uh, and, uh, doing pretty good and getting more ideas on my own and just about how to go about it. Uh, it's, it's just, it's just something I really like. This, uh, this music is, uh, something that, uh, it's appealing to me. Uh, I performed for some, uh, some of the, uh, big delegates. Uh, down around New Orleans East, back there. And, well, I, I met the guys, uh, shook their hand and talked to them for a while. But, uh, and just say, keep up the good work.
